convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in MT5 close price comparisons (iClose wrapper), no custom indicators, simple breakout entry/exit logic, fixed SL/TP with pip adjustment, standard MoneyFixedMargin money management from MT5 Standard Library. All dependencies are standard MT5 library .mqh files, no external custom indicators.

params.adjustment: multiplied by digits_adjust for 3/5 digit brokers
multiplied by digits_adjust for 3/5 digit brokers

other_exits: Closes opposite side positions before entering new trade (e.g. closes SELL positions before opening BUY when breakout triggers)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Uses CMoneyFixedMargin (MoneyFixedMargin.mqh) which calculates lot size based on PercentRisk (10%) of margin. The CheckOpenLong/CheckOpenShort methods compute the lot size dynamically. If the computed lot is 0.0, trade is skipped. The 'Lots' input parameter exists but is NOT used in the actual order sending - only the money manager's computed lot is used.

custom_logic_notes: Hedging account required (ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING). The EA checks if both Buys and Sells inputs are false at init and fails if so. Entry is a simple price level breakout: when previous bar's close crosses above the AppPrice level, a BUY is triggered; when it crosses below, a SELL is triggered. The crossover detection uses bar index 1 (previous completed bar) vs bar index 2 (two bars back) compared to the static AppPrice level, effectively acting as a new-bar guard since close[1] only changes when a new bar completes. Opposite positions are closed before opening a new position. The 'Lots' input (0.1) is declared but never referenced in trade execution - lot sizing is entirely controlled by CMoneyFixedMargin.CheckOpenLong/CheckOpenShort which uses PercentRisk=10%.
python_conversion_notes: Straightforward breakout strategy. Key points for conversion: (1) The digit adjustment (multiply SL/TP by 10 for 5-digit brokers) must be replicated by checking the symbol's point value. (2) The CMoneyFixedMargin class calculates lot size based on fixed margin percentage - this needs to be reimplemented or replaced with a simpler risk-based lot calculation. (3) The iClose(1) and iClose(2) refer to the previous bar and two bars back respectively - this is the signal basis (previous bar close vs static price level). (4) The hedging check is MT5-specific and can be omitted in Python. (5) No custom indicators to port - only price level comparison logic. (6) AppPrice is a user-defined static price level (not an indicator), so the breakout level must be provided as a parameter. (7) Position counting by magic number and symbol must be replicated for position_gate logic.
